content.title: How to Study the Seerah? || Key Takeaways from Ansar Special Webinar 03
content.subtitle: Let the study of the Seerah return to every home, just like Quran learning.
content.body:
The renowned Tabi‘i Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, RA) said, “We used to teach our children the battles and Seerah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the same care with which we taught them the Quran.” (Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya, Vol. 4, p. 293)

Looking back at our childhood, were our families and teachers equally eager to teach us the Seerah and the Quran?

Allah Almighty declares in the Holy Quran that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the best example for us. But how can we follow someone we do not know? In Ansar Special Webinar 03, speaker Kabir Anwar shared practical guidance on making Seerah study simple, consistent, and effective. Here are the key takeaways.

Start with Short and Easy-to-Read Books

Starting with a massive encyclopedia can overwhelm readers and discourage them. Instead, begin with short, engaging books such as Zakaria Masud’s Amar Nabi Muhammad, Mufti Muhammad Shafi’s Sirat Khatam al-Anbiya, or Tomake Bhalobashi He Nabi, written by Gurudatta Singh and translated by Mawlana Abu Taher Misbah.

After building a foundation, gradually explore more comprehensive works, including Raindrops’ two-volume Seerah, Dr. Ali al-Sallabi’s Seerah, and Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum.

Understand the Historical Background

Reading the Seerah requires more than knowing what happened; understanding the historical context is equally important.

For example, Abu Jahl and other Quraysh leaders secretly listened to the Prophet ﷺ reciting the Quran. Although they recognized its truth, tribal pride and rivalry over leadership prevented them from accepting Islam. These conflicts had roots in earlier generations. Understanding the background makes Seerah events more vivid and meaningful.

Connect the Seerah to Everyday Life

The Seerah is a practical guide for everyday life. Discuss events from the Prophet’s ﷺ life with your children and ask them, “What would you do in such a situation?”

Learn how he managed his family, treated relatives, and showed patience toward his Ummah. Apply these qualities in your own family. For specific religious rulings, however, seek guidance from qualified scholars rather than relying on personal interpretations.

Exercise caution when reading Seerah books by Orientalist or non-Muslim authors. Consult knowledgeable scholars before choosing them to avoid potentially misleading interpretations.

Focus on Events, Not Dates

Do not begin by memorizing battle dates or genealogies. Instead, focus on the sequence of events, their lessons, and the Prophet’s ﷺ character. With consistent reading, names and dates will gradually become familiar.

Make Seerah a Family Tradition

Every household should develop the habit of studying the Seerah alongside Quran learning. Many illustrated Seerah books with simple explanations are available for children.

Choose books suited to their ages and interests. Keep them in your living room and on their reading tables. Let these books nurture love for the Prophet ﷺ from an early age.

Opportunities for Structured Study

Those seeking a systematic approach can consider Kabir Anwar’s year-long Seerah course at Itqaan Institute (https://itqaan.org/).

The course includes:

  • 80 live classes

  • 80 examinations

  • 3 term examinations

Begin Your Family’s Journey at the Book Fair

The Islamic book fair is currently underway at the East Gate of Baitul Mukarram National Mosque in Dhaka. It offers books for all ages, including illustrated Seerah series for children, books on Asma’ul Husna and Allah’s attributes, and other Islamic titles.

The fair also features a special Seerah Corner, showcasing historical scenes of Makkah and Madinah through an exhibition that brings the Prophet’s ﷺ era closer to children.

Visit the fair with your family. Buy books, read together, and make reading aloud a habit. Nurture love for the Prophet ﷺ in your children so they may grow into righteous individuals whose goodness becomes a means of your salvation in the Hereafter.

Book Fair Hours: Daily, 12:00 PM–9:00 PM; on holidays, 10:00 AM–10:00 PM.
